analysis.title: Inside Commodities - October 29, 2026
key_insights: China issued a fourth batch of fuel export quotas (gasoline, diesel, jet fuel) of about 3.7 million to nearly 4 million metric tons, mostly to state-owned majors. This brings the 2026 total to roughly 40 million tons, flat y/y, after a third batch of 4.55 million tons earlier in October.

Rising Chinese fuel supply is expected to weigh on Asian fundamentals near term. LSEG data showed front-month diesel and jet fuel paper timespreads at their lowest since end-June, which reflects more prompt supply relative to the forward month.

Beijing began curbing fuel exports in March as the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted oil flows and refinery output in the Middle East and Asia. Curbs were relaxed July to September, and shipments are now vetted month by month.
CPC Blend exports are planned to fall 2% in November from October to about 6.4 million tons (1.69 million bpd). Record Black Sea freight rates and security risks keep exports challenging.

CPC system exports fell to 1.5 million bpd in September from 1.6 million bpd in August on Karachaganak maintenance. Jan 1 to Sep 25 shipments were almost 50 million tons, down 4 million tons y/y, after Ukrainian drone attacks on the terminal and tankers.

The EU anti-deforestation regulation (EUDR) starts December 30. FEFAC warns traceability rules could shut out up to 4 million tons of Brazilian soymeal, about 17% of Brazil's exports. Brazil is about half of EU soymeal imports and exported a record 23.3 million tons in 2025.

Argentina, the largest soymeal exporter at about 27 million tons last year, says it can fill a 5 to 6 million ton gap. FEFAC rates Argentina and Paraguay 'low' risk for EUDR disruption and Brazil 'medium'.

Russia shipped grain through Murmansk for the first time, a 3,400 ton first load plus about 28,000 tons of wheat bound for Casablanca. The Black Sea trade has been at a standstill since July because of attacks on ports and vessels, and Baltic ports handled 1.2 million tons in September, over 60% of seaborne grain exports.

Russia issued permits for grain vessels to leave the Sea of Azov through Kerch Strait for the first time since July 10, valid through November 15, with naval convoy escort for some. This coincided with a localized ceasefire in the Kherson region.

The LME is exploring tokenising off-warrant metal inventories in Hong Kong warehouses to support financing, linked to Hong Kong's five-year plan. An invitation-only roundtable is set for early November. On-warrant metal is excluded.

Fund positioning in LME zinc is at record shorts and near-record longs. ILZSG now sees an 88,000 ton deficit in 2026, versus a 271,000 ton surplus forecast a year earlier, because mined output is on track to fall 2.6% in 2026.

China is in zinc surplus (refined output +3.7%) while the rest of the world contracts 2.0%. China exported 111,000 tons of refined zinc in August and September, the largest volume in 20 years. LME stocks recovered from 92,550 to 165,650 tons, but cancellations are rising and the cash premium over 3-month zinc widened from under $50 to $118 per ton.

Three-month LME zinc bounced from $3,650 on October 15 to a Tuesday high of $3,855. ILZSG expects 3.0% mined supply growth and a 25,000 ton surplus in 2027, a marginal call in a 14 million ton market.

Dutch TTF front-month gas touched €100.10/MWh, the first time since December 2022, on Houthi attacks on a Saudi refinery and QatarEnergy extending LNG force majeure to end-December. Low German storage, Norwegian flow disruptions and colder, calmer weather add to demand.
Citi sees the TTF winter 2026-27 spread at €85/MWh with Middle East escalation and about €154/MWh if LNG facilities are hit. EU carbon rose €1.10 to €89.15 per ton.

MARAD approved the deepwater port license for the $8.2 billion ST LNG project (8.4 mtpa, offshore Matagorda, Texas). Construction is expected to begin in 2027 and start-up in 2029. The review took 410 days, and PHMSA proposed rules to speed LNG projects.
Jordan bought about 60,000 tons of feed barley at an estimated $295.25/t c&f from Al Ghurair for first-half January 2027 shipment. A new 120,000 ton tender is expected to close November 4.

tension_points.bull_case: ILZSG sees an 88,000 ton 2026 deficit as mined output falls 2.6%, cash premium widened to $118 per ton, cancellations are rising and off-warrant stocks are only 11,261 tons.
tension_points.bear_case: China's record refined exports are rebuilding LME stocks, demand is barely growing, and ILZSG forecasts a 25,000 ton surplus in 2027 as mine supply grows 3.0%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Chinese export pace failing to continue, since Chinese smelters are struggling to access raw material and concentrate imports grew only 0.6% y/y in the first nine months of 2026.

theme_stances.key_argument: Record long and short fund positions leave no price consensus, and the bull-bear battle looks set to continue.
theme_stances.evidence: there is still everything to fight for

theme_stances.key_argument: Limited Middle East exports, Norwegian disruptions, low German storage and colder weather push TTF to €100.
